verdict.rationale: Restate documents a multi-node cluster server, recovery of in-progress invocations after infrastructure crashes, and services that can be scaled independently as containers or Kubernetes pods. That covers worker-loss tolerance and implies horizontal scale-out, but no evidence describes how the server distributes tasks across a fleet of service workers or shows throughput scaling as workers are added. Missing for 10: explicit load-balancing of invocations across worker instances, documented throughput scaling from adding workers, independent or hands-on corroboration of fleet-level failover.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, throughput scales by adding workers — the platform load-balances tasks across the fleet and tolerates worker loss

citations.quote: Restate is distributed as a single binary that implements all features required to run a single- or multi-node cluster
Deploy complex tool logic as separate durable services. Scale tools independently, use any language, and get end-to-end durability.
Automatically retry transient errors like infrastructure crashes and network failures
Code automatically stores completed steps and resumes from where it left off when recovering from failures.
The Restate Server will proxy all requests for these services.
